comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 published curriculum (later detailed programme not yet determined)
comparator.sourceNotes: Radboud lists ten compulsory 6-EC year-one courses. From year two, students choose Accounting, Finance or International Economics & Policy. This representative route retains the broad economics and policy identity; its year-two path comprises ten listed compulsory 6-EC courses. The applicable year-three route has four compulsory 6-EC specialist courses, four restricted 6-EC electives (24 EC), and a required 12-EC economics thesis. The elective space is explicitly restricted, not invented free electives. The year-three page states that its detail applies through 2026–2027 and later cohorts are not yet determined; this is a comparison of the currently published pathway, not a guaranteed 2028–2029 schedule.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad route, five actual substitutions replace specialist banking, mathematical statistics, consumer marketing and organisational psychology with commercial regulation, environmental foundations, international politics and social/environmental justice. These choices serve the evidenced policy and responsible-business question, not numerical variety.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target contains three current specialisations. International Economics and Policy covers economic theory, international markets, sustainability, inequality and policy and therefore best represents the degree’s broad academic economics identity. Accounting and Finance are more sector-specific; this choice was made from Radboud’s stated programme, independent of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest UCR response retains economic theory, finance, business and quantitative research. The second route shifts five substantive courses toward economic policy, responsible firms and sustainability. Both remain feasible and differ by five courses each. Separate specialist finance and accounting routes are evidenced but cannot form credible distinct 24-course programmes from the current UCR offer without weak substitutes.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Matched explicitly after semantic review: Introduction to Economics and the Economy corresponds to Introduction to Economics.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Macroeconomics corresponds to International Macroeconomics.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Microeconomics corresponds to Microeconomics & Behavior.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Behavioural and Experimental Economics corresponds to Behavioral Economics.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Public Economics and Finance corresponds to Public Economics.
No included UCR course directly treats development economics as an economic subfield.
Sociology and public economics touch inequality but do not directly teach labour economics.
General market strategy and behavioural economics do not replace a dedicated game-theory course.
Modern history and business study do not directly teach the disciplinary history of economic thought.

Matched explicitly after semantic review: Applied Methods in Economics and Policy corresponds to Introduction to Data Science.

UCR has one econometrics course aligned to the first applied sequence; no separately credited second stage appears.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Introduction to Business and Finance corresponds to Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Accounting & Control (EN) corresponds to Accounting & Corporate Finance.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Corporate Finance corresponds to Money, Banking & Finance.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Introduction to Marketing and Strategy corresponds to Marketing & Consumer Engagement.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Markets and Strategy corresponds to Strategy & Digital Transformation.
The UCR banking/finance course does not separately reproduce international financial policy.
UCR studies environmental governance and impacts, but no scheduled course directly teaches the economics of sustainability at Radboud’s scope.
The UCR macroeconomics course already aligns to Radboud macroeconomics; global business is not a direct substitute for international economic theory.
No single scheduled course covers the advanced topical seminar in international economics and policy as such.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Academic and Professional skills corresponds to Personal & Professional Development.
Radboud restricts four six-credit elective choices to its programme list; UCR courses have their own separately represented curriculum.
Radboud requires a twelve-credit economics thesis; UCR independent research appears only as a comparison-only option.

notes.text: Radboud provides a dedicated multi-year economics and business-economics curriculum with a named specialisation, staged econometrics and a required economics thesis. UCR combines its economics, business, quantitative, policy and sustainability courses flexibly, but these programmes do not reproduce Radboud’s disciplinary depth or mandatory thesis.
